newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WMC phosphate project aimed at Asia market.
newsitem.headline: WMC phosphate project aimed at Asia market.

text.p: Western Mining Corp Ltd said nearly half the high-analysis fertiliser production at its new A$750 million Phosphate Hill mine in the state of Queensland would be aimed at Asian and New Zealand markets.

"The domestic product will peak and require us to have exports. About 40 to 50 percent (of production) is going offshore," Ross McCann, executive general manager projects at WMC Resources Ltd told a gas conference.

The project, being developed near Mt Isa in north-west Queensland, was proceeding following supply agreements including a guaranteed natural gas supply to produce ammonia, an ingredient of superphosphate, McCann said.
"It is a key ingredient in this process. Natural gas was essential to Phosphate Hill proceeding," he said.
Products from the mine would be value-added from basic phosphate rock which commanded only A$45 a tonne on world markets to ammonium phosphate which was worth A$300 a tonne, McCann said.
"This project is about value-adding. High analysis fertiliser at least doubles the nutrient content of single superphosphate," he said.
Annual production rising to about 1.25 million tonnes a year and sold through WMC subsidiary Hi-Fert Pty Ltd would be a A$300 million to A$400 million a year import replacement, McCann said.
